title: Port Morris Industrial Business Zone
link_text: Port Morris Industrial Business Zone - presented to Bronx Community Board 1 in June 2026 (pdf)
description: As part of the NYC DOT Truck Route Network Redesign, East 141st Street, East 140th Street, East 135th Street, Brook Avenue, St. Ann's Avenue, Walnut Avenue, and Locust Avenue will be added as new local truck routes in the Port Morris Industrial Business Zone (IBZ) area. These planned additions will better formalize truck activity in the area, support truck route enforcement, help keep trucks off residential streets, and facilitate truck access to and from the IBZ. To complement these route additions, NYC DOT is proposing several safety enhancements, including converting Locust Avenue and Walnut Avenue into a one-way pair, implementing traffic calming measures at high-crash intersections, adding pedestrian safety improvements throughout the project area, improving curb management to reduce sidewalk parking, and enhancing circulation for truck access and egress within the IBZ.

title: Westchester Avenue, Waters Avenue to Middletown Road
link_text: Westchester Avenue, Waters Avenue to Middletown Road - presented to Councilmember Aldebol in April 2026 (pdf)
description: This school safety project aims to improve safety for students on Westchester Avenue, and Waters Place in the vicinity of P721X, a school serving students with various disabilities. NYC DOT is proposing to install five painted curb extensions along Westchester Avenue at Waters Avenue, Waters Place, and Hutchinson River Parkway East; to signalize two slip lanes at Westchester Avenue and Waters Place; to add Leading Pedestrian Intervals at Westchester Avenue and Waters Place and at Westchester Avenue and Hutchinson River Parkway East; to add a dedicated left turn signal phase for eastbound vehicles on Westchester Avenue at Hutchinson River Parkway East; to remove redundant left turn lanes from Fink Avenue at Waters Place and from Waters Place at Westchester Avenue; and to ban left turns from westbound Westchester Avenue at Hutchinson River Parkway East. The project will encourage slower turning speeds in front of a school and an elevated subway station, simplify traffic patterns, and provide shorter crossing distances and additional pedestrian space. Although designed primarily to improve safety for students, this project will improve safety for New Yorkers of all ages.

title: Adams Street & Boerum Place
link_text: Adams Street & Boerum Place - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 2 in June 2026 (pdf)
description: The Adams Street and Boerum Place street improvement projects seeks to improve access, circulation and safety for cyclists to and from the Brooklyn Bridge bike path. The Brooklyn Bridge is a major connection for cyclists between Brooklyn and Manhattan and has seen cycling volumes increase over the years. Within the past 10 years to improve the connections for cyclists and pedestrians to and from the Brooklyn Bridge a shared cycling and walking path was constructed between Johnson Street and Tillary Street. This project seeks to continue a two-way bike lane between Johnson Street and Bergen Street. For the majority of the two-way bike lane, the alignment will be center running along the east side of the landscape median between Johnson Street and Schermerhorn Street. Due to connection challenges at Atlantic Avenue, the alignment of two-way bike lane will move to the west side of the street between Schermerhorn Street and Bergen Street. Installation of the two-way bike lane will follow the repaving of the street in the fall 2026; however, due to construction activity south of Atlantic Avenue, the repaving for this section will be held until a future year.

title: Albany Avenue, Troy Avenue, Bergen Street, and Park Place
link_text: Albany Avenue, Troy Avenue, Bergen Street, and Park Place - Street Design Checklist (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements around the NYCHA Albany Houses campus on Albany Avenue, Park Place, Troy Avenue, and Bergen Street, Brooklyn. This School Safety project would serve residents and 2,500+ students who attend six local schools. On Albany Avenue, the proposal includes a protected bike lane and a narrowed moving lane to calm traffic and reduce speeding. On Troy Avenue, this proposal features a painted sidewalk extension along the entire NYCHA block to narrow the existing moving lanes, reduce speeding, and shorten crosswalks. Pedestrian accessibility and safety would be further enhanced by the addition of painted curb extensions on the intersections, a new traffic signal at Albany Avenue and Prospect Place, and a new stop-controlled midblock crosswalk on Park Place between MS 354, KIPP AMP Charter School, and the NYCHA Albany Houses.

title: Ashland Place, Lafayette Avenue & Hanson Place
link_text: Ashland Place & Hanson Place - Street Design Checklist (pdf)
description: In 2023, NYC DOT installed a two-way protected bike lane on Navy Street and Ashland Place between Flushing Avenue and Lafayette Avenue to calm traffic and provide a safer route between the Manhattan Bridge, Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway, and Downtown and Central Brooklyn. In 2026, NYC DOT is proposing to connect the Ashland Place bike lane to the 4th Avenue and Schermerhorn Street bike lanes. This project will convert Ashland Place between Hanson Place and Lafayette Avenue and Hanson Place between St Felix Street and Ashland Place from two-way streets to one-way northbound and add a new protected bike lane to Ashland Place. Hanson Place will be a shared street with a eastbound bike lane and westbound shared bike route.

title: Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway
link_text: Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway Presentation (pdf)
description: The Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway is a planned 14-mile pedestrian and bicycle route connecting communities along Brooklyn’s waterfront. Separate paths for bicycles and pedestrians will allow cyclists and walkers to commute, exercise, explore, and relax from Newtown Creek in north Brooklyn to the beginning of the Shore Parkway Greenway in Bay Ridge, creating a full 27-mile greenway along Brooklyn’s waterfront. The Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway is a trunk segment in New York City’s expanding network of greenways, which includes the Manhattan Waterfront Greenway, the Queens East River Greenway, the Shore Parkway Greenway, and the Jamaica Bay Greenway. Over the past decade, New York City has truly opened public access to the waterfront with over 60 miles of public space planned or under construction. The completion of the Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway is a crucial part of this vision. Several segments of the Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway are already in place and include some of the most popular bicycle and pedestrian routes in the City. Altogether, this unique set of pathways, green spaces, and public programs is transforming Brooklyn’s waterfront.

title: Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway: Commercial Street, West Street to Manhattan Avenue
link_text: BWG Implementation Plan , and as part of the ongoing multi-agency efforts to expand the
description: NYC DOT, in partnership with the Department of Design and Construction is implementing a capital project to complete a segment of the Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway (BWG) along Commercial Street in Greenpoint, between West Street and Manhattan Avenue. First identified as part of the BWG Implementation Plan , and as part of the ongoing multi-agency efforts to expand the NYC Greenways network, this project includes construction of a new off-street greenway, traffic direction changes, and pedestrian safety improvements. Once completed, the project will extend the greenway to its northern terminus and provide a protected path for cyclists and other Greenway users. Commercial Street and Box Street will be converted to one-way operations within the project limits in order to create a consistent corridor, simplify traffic patterns, and reduce conflicts while accommodating dedicated space for cycling and walking. The project will also include new sidewalk extensions, ADA-compliant pedestrian ramps, upgraded crossings, and a new stop control and crosswalks at the intersection of Commercial Street and Box Street to improve pedestrian safety and accessibility. This project will also include additional streetscape enhancements such as landscaping, green infrastructure, WalkNYC wayfinding signage, and other street furniture, as well as sewer and water main upgrades.

title: DUMBO Bike Network Expansion

Improvements include new conventional and protected bicycle lanes, a new two-way protected bicycle lane on Front Street, and enhanced connections to existing bicycle infrastructure. Vehicle capacity will remain unchanged, while a limited amount of parking will be removed where necessary to improve safety and visibility.

title: Flatlands Avenue, Pennsylvania Avenue to Fountain Avenue
link_text: Flatlands Avenue, Pennsylvania Avenue to Fountain Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 5 in April 2026 (pdf)
description: As part of the Truck Route Network Redesign, NYC DOT plans to add Flatlands Avenue, from Pennsylvania Avenue to Fountain Avenue, as a local truck route. This planned route addition will support efforts to keep larger trucks off narrow residential streets adjacent to Flatlands Avenue and facilitate commercial vehicle access to/from the Flatlands/Fairfield Industrial Business Zone, Gateway Mall area, and other adjacent freight related land uses. NYC DOT is proposing safety enhancements to complement this route addition, including implementation of traffic calming at high-crash intersections, adding pedestrian safety enhancements throughout the corridor, and improving signal timing at select intersections.

title: Hamilton Avenue & Third Avenue
link_text: Hamilton Ave & 3rd Ave - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 7 in December 2014 (pdf)
description: Hamilton Ave and 3rd Ave, between Smith St and 29th St is currently being redesigned by NYC DOT and the Department of Design and Construction as part of a capital reconstruction project. Construction is expected to begin in Fall 2019, reconstructing the south bound portion of the roadway to encompass additional pedestrian amenities and a protected two-way bike path. This project builds another segment of the Brooklyn Waterfront Greenway, moving closer to NYC DOT’s vision of a continuous greenway facility along Brooklyn’s western waterfront, connecting Greenpoint to Owl’s Head Park in Sunset Park.

title: Hillel Plaza, Kenilworth Place to Nostrand Avenue
link_text: Hillel Plaza, Kenilworth Place to Nostrand Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 14 Transportation Committee in May 2026 (pdf)
description: Flatbush Junction sees thousands of pedestrians daily as it sits at the intersection of a major commercial, transit, culture, and education hub. In 2015, the Flatbush Junction BID applied to NYC DOT’s Plaza Program to create a pedestrian plaza on Hillel Place between Kenilworth Place and Nostrand Avenue. The pedestrian plaza created much needed pedestrian space at this bustling intersection by creating a space where shoppers, students, and residents alike can find a place to sit, study, or socialize. The plaza is now included in a capital reconstruction project in conjunction with NYC DDC. The permanent plaza will include new paving materials, trees, landscaping and lighting.

title: Marcy Avenue, Borinquen Place to Broadway
link_text: Marcy Avenue, Borinquen Place to Broadway - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 1 in September 2025 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT recently installed a bus priority lane along the three blocks of Marcy Avenue between Borinquen Place and Broadway. These three blocks host a confluence of three Williamsburg Bridge/Washington Plaza-bound bus routes: the B24, B60, and Q54, and each route experiences delays and slower speeds along this tail end stretch. These delays compound on top of delays earlier in the routes’ journeys and result in buses arriving late to their terminal, delaying the next scheduled run. NYC DOT installed a bus priority lane along these three blocks of Marcy Avenue to help alleviate these delays and is monitoring and evaluating its impact through the end of the year.

title: McGuinness Boulevard, Calyer Street to Freeman Street
link_text: McGuinness Boulevard, Calyer Street to Freeman Street - Street Design Checklist (pdf)
description: NYC DOT and Assembly Member Emily Gallagher hosted workshops in 2021 to discuss safety improvements along McGuinness Boulevard, from Meeker Avenue to Ash Street, in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. In June of 2022, NYC DOT presented the information learned from community member’s feedback, along with options for how the street can be redesigned for a safer corridor. In 2023 and 2024 NYC DOT installed two different designs along the corridor. In 2026, NYC DOT presented an updated design of McGuinness Boulevard between Cayler Street and Freeman Street to match the parking protected design south of Calyer Street that was installed in 2024 to narrow both sides of the roadway to provide space for people walking and biking.

title: Myrtle Wyckoff Plaza and Wyckoff Avenue Corridor Safety Improvements
link_text: Wyckoff Avenue Intersection & Plaza Corridor Safety Improvements - presented in November 2024
description: Three pedestrian fatalities between 2009 and 2014 occurred at this complicated six-leg intersection on the border of Brooklyn and Queens, at the bustling Myrtle/Wyckoff transportation hub. In 2014, NYC DOT implemented five turn bans which saw low compliance. In 2016, new Vision Zero safety funding presented an opportunity to further simplify the intersection. The 2016 project converted Wyckoff Avenue between Gates and Myrtle into a pedestrian plaza, which allowed pedestrians to make subway to bus connections without crossing the street and created a central neighborhood public space where the Myrtle Avenue and Wyckoff Avenue retail corridors intersect. In conjunction with NYC DDC, NYC DOT is planning to construct the temporary plaza in permanent materials as part of a larger NYC DEP sewer and water main replacement project. The permanent plaza will feature additional street furnishings, pedestrian scale lighting, and landscaping.

title: New Utrecht Avenue & 10th Avenue
link_text: New Utrecht Avenue and 10th Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 12 in September 2022 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing pedestrian safety and comfort enhancements to the intersection of New Utrecht Avenue, 10th Avenue, and 41st Street in Brooklyn. The proposal includes four new crosswalks, a concrete pedestrian island in the middle of the intersection, and a painted pedestrian space with flexible delineators at the southern end of the intersection. The proposed project creates new pedestrian crossings aligned with the pedestrian desire lines within the intersection and helps clarify movements for both drivers and pedestrians. In addition, the project reduces the crossing distances and creates safer, shorter pedestrian crossings.

title: New Utrecht Avenue and 17th Avenue, 78th Street to 81st Street
link_text: New Utrecht Avenue and 17th Avenue, 78th Street to 81st Street - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 11 in June 2026 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements on New Utrecht Avenue and 17th Avenue between 78th Street and 81st Street. This School Safety project intends to serve the 3,300+ students who attend New Utrecht High School. NYC DOT proposes simplifying the complex bowtie intersection of New Utrecht Avenue and 17th Avenue at 79th Street by converting 17th Avenue to one-way northbound between 79th Street and 78th Street and one-way southbound between 79th Street to 80th Street. These conversions allow for additional pedestrian safety improvements at the intersection, including closing the slip lane from 17th Avenue onto New Utrecht Avenue, installing a concrete pedestrian island, and expanding the sidewalk on the triangle at 17th Avenue and 80th Street. Additionally, the proposal includes new signals and crosswalks on New Utrecht Avenue at 78th Street and 81st Street to improve traffic flow and enhance pedestrian safety. Finally, the proposal includes painted and concrete curb extensions throughout to improve visibility, shorten pedestrian crossing distances, and slow turning vehicles.

title: New Utrecht Avenue, 54th/55th Streets & 60th/61st Streets
link_text: New Utrecht Avenue, 13th, & 14th Avenues at 54th/55th Streets & 60th/61st Streets - What's Happening Here? Flyer
description: NYC DOT is proposing intersection safety improvements on New Utrecht Avenue at the intersections of 54th Street, 55th Street, 60th Street and 61st Street in Brooklyn. The project consists of intersection safety treatments that will improve roadway organization and pedestrian safety. The project proposes a raised crosswalk at 54th Street as well as multiple new crosswalks with improved pedestrian refuge space to help create shorter, safer crossings and help improve pedestrian visibility at these busy intersections.

title: Park Avenue - Ingersoll Houses
link_text: Park Avenue - Ingersoll Houses - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 2 in January 2026 (pdf)
description: As part of an upcoming capital project, NYC DOT will provide critical pedestrian and cyclist safety improvements in the form of: two slip lane closures at the southwest and southeast corners of Tillary Street, Park Avenue, and Navy Street intersection; a bus bulb and bus pad for the B62 bus; targeted sidewalk reconstruction; raised bike lanes along part of Navy Street; replacement of the vehicular crossover at Park Avenue and St. Edwards Street with new pedestrian space; and installation of the ADA-compliant pedestrian ramps throughout the project limits.

title: Park Avenue – Crossover, Grand Avenue
link_text: Park Avenue – Crossover - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 4 Transportation Committee in December 2023
description: As part of an upcoming capital project, NYC DOT will provide critical pedestrian safety improvements on Park Avenue at Grand Avenue and Ryerson Street. New crossings and traffic signals as well as improved geometry will be create at both intersections. A new thru street will be created at Ryerson Street and the under elevated spaces at Grand Avenue will be reorganized and consolidated. Throughout the project, sidewalks will be reconstructed and new curbs, street trees, and water infrastructure will be added. Installation of ADA-compliant pedestrian ramps will be included throughout the project limits.

title: Park Avenue, Broadway to Nostrand Avenue
link_text: Park Avenue, Broadway to Nostrand Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 3 in June 2025
description: NYC DOT is proposing Vision Zero safety improvements on Park Avenue, from Broadway to Nostrand Avenue, in Brooklyn. Proposed improvements include installing painted curb extensions and a buffered parking lane. Safety benefits of these treatments include shorter and safer pedestrian crossings, improved roadway organization with safer travel speeds, and slower, safer turns. The surrounding project area includes major pedestrian destinations, including 5+ schools, numerous transit stops, Woodhull Hospital, and NYCHA Marcy, Tompkins, and Sumner Houses.

title: Red Hook Traffic & Truck Study
link_text: Red Hook Traffic & Truck Study - Kickoff Meeting in March 2023
description: NYC DOT is conducting an Area-Wide 18-month Traffic & Truck Study for the Red Hook neighborhood, collaborating with DCP, NYNJPA, and EDC. The Red Hook area is experiencing significant land use changes, largely influenced by the growing e-commerce industry. As a waterfront area with historical industrial uses, it has become attractive for the placement of last-mile warehouses. The study which seeks to address community issues and concerns will comprehensively examine traffic and truck issues in the neighborhood and assess the effects of increased traffic to the extent possible. The approximately 1.2 sq-miles study area is bounded by: Buttermilk Channel/Degraw Street to the North, Gowanus Bay/19th Street/3rd Avenue to the South, Red Hook Channel to the West and Hamilton Avenue/Brooklyn-Queens Expressway to the East.

title: Remsen Avenue, Seaview Avenue to Avenue B
link_text: Remsen Avenue Safety Improvements - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 18 in June 2019 (pdf)
description: Following community requests for traffic calming on Remsen Avenue, the NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements on Remsen Avenue between Seaview Avenue and Avenue B. The project will include the removal of one travel lane in each direction on segments of the corridor where it is feasible. This design will include the installation of painted curb extensions at Flatbush Avenue, new signal timing and a dedicated southbound left turn lane at Remsen Avenue and Glenwood Road. In addition, the design will include bike lanes along the corridor. These safety improvements will work to address safety at the Vision Zero intersection on Flatlands Avenue and Remsen Avenue, discourage the observed speeding along the corridor, provide safer pedestrian crossings and organize the roadway for vehicles, cyclists and pedestrians.

title: Rochester Avenue, East New York Avenue to Fulton Street
link_text: Rochester Avenue, East New York Avenue to Fulton Street - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 8 in June 2025
description: Rochester Avenue is a Vision Zero and Truck Priority Safety corridor with multiple crashes along the corridor involving trucks and vulnerable road users (pedestrians and cyclists). This project aims to improve safety for all road users by providing safer and shorter crossings with painted curb extensions, installing a new enhanced crossing near Lincoln Terrace / Arthur S. Somers Park, calming traffic by design, explore modifications in signal timing, and improving curb management by strategically adding neighborhood loading zones at select locations.

title: Sands Street, Jay Street to Adams Street & Adams Street, Sands Street to Front Street
link_text: Sands Street, Jay Street to Adams Street & Adams Street, Sands Street to Front Street - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 2 in September 2026 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing bicycle and pedestrian safety improvements along Sands Street and Adams Street following street repaving in 2027. The project will upgrade existing bicycle facilities, including protected bicycle lanes on Sands Street and Adams Street, a conventional bicycle lane on Adams Street between York Street and Front Street, and a protected bicycle lane with a floating parking lane on Sands Street between Pearl Street and Adams Street. Daylighting will be added at key intersections to improve visibility and turning movements. These improvements will strengthen connections to the surrounding bicycle network, improve safety and accessibility, and provide more comfortable routes for people biking while maintaining vehicle capacity.

title: Seventh Avenue & Eighth Avenue, 39th Street to 66th Street
link_text: Seventh Avenue & Eighth Avenue, 39th Street to 66th Street - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 7 in October 2021 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing Vision Zero safety improvements on Seventh and Eighth Avenues between 39th Street and 66th Street. This Vision Zero complete streets project will convert Seventh and Eighth Avenues into one-way pairs and install Protected Bike Lanes, expand pedestrian space, and provide improved curbside management. This proposal aims to increase safety on a Vision Zero Priority Corridor as well as improve mobility for all roadway users along the corridors.

link_text: Third Avenue, Wakeman Place to 86th Street - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 10 in May 2026 (pdf)
description: As part of the Truck Route Network Redesign, NYC DOT plans to add 3rd Avenue, from Wakeman Place to 86th Street, as a local truck route. This planned route addition will support efforts to keep larger trucks off narrow residential streets adjacent to 3rd Avenue and facilitate commercial vehicle access to/from the corridor. NYC DOT is proposing safety enhancements to complement this route addition, including implementation of traffic calming at high-crash intersections, adding pedestrian safety enhancements throughout the corridor, improving curb management to reduce instances of double parking, and improving signal timing at select intersections.

title: Times Plaza
link_text: Times Plaza - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 2 Transportation Committee in May 2017 (pdf)
description: At the intersection of Flatbush Avenue, Fourth Avenue, and Atlantic Avenue, Times Plaza is a bustling meeting point of three corridors. Times Plaza was expanded in asphalt following the development of Barclays Center and is now slated to be redesigned to create an enhanced, permanent public space. NYC DOT, Greenland Forest City, and Stantec presented a preliminary plan to the public on Wednesday, 1/27/16, and will incorporate feedback received before presenting to Community Board 2.

title: Truxton Street, Mother Gaston Boulevard, Eastern Parkway
link_text: Truxton Street, Mother Gaston Boulevard, Eastern Parkway - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 16 in May 2026 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing traffic safety improvements on Truxton Street, Mother Gaston Boulevard, and Eastern Parkway around Imagine Me Leadership Charter School, located near Broadway Junction in Brooklyn. The proposal includes the closure of Truxton Street between Eastern Parkway and Mother Gaston Boulevard, the conversion of Mother Gaston Boulevard to a southbound one-way between Somers Street and Truxton Street, a 15-mph school slow zone and chicanes along Mother Gaston Boulevard, painted curb extensions, installation of jersey barriers along the Eastern Parkway median, and an NYC DOT Art mural installation. Together, these improvements will reduce vehicle speeds, prevent dangerous turning movements, improve visibility at crosswalks, and create a safer, more welcoming pedestrian environment for the students and families who travel through this area each day.

title: Union Street, Van Brunt Street to Third Avenue
link_text: Union Street, Van Brunt Street to Third Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 6 in May 2025
description: NYC DOT is proposing bicycle network improvements on Union Street between Van Brunt Street and Third Avenue. The proposed improvements include a two-way parking protected bike lane between Bond Street and Third Avenue, and a redesign of the existing conventional bike lane to better align with rest of the proposal. The project aims to organize the roadway and provided cyclists with a safer connection across the Gowanus Canal.

title: Woodhull Street/Hamilton Avenue
link_text: Woodhull Street/Hamilton Avenue - presented to Brooklyn Community Board 6 in May 2026 (pdf)
description: The Woodhull Street/Hamilton Avenue street improvement project seeks to improve pedestrian safety and accessibility and reduce weaving and speeding on Hamilton Avenue westbound and eastbound from Hicks Street to Woodhull Street in Red Hook Brooklyn. The proposed project includes lane reductions, street direction changes, curb extensions, traffic delineators, a new traffic signal and several new stop controlled pedestrian crossings.

title: 116th Street, Morningside Avenue to Pleasant Avenue
link_text: 116th Street, Morningside Avenue to Pleasant Avenue - Street Design Checklist (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is studying bus priority and pedestrian safety improvements on 116th Street, Manhattan Avenue, Morningside Avenue and Pleasant Avenue in Manhattan. The 116th Street Study Area serves 10 bus routes (M3, M7, M102, M116, BxM1, BxM6, BxM7, BxM8, BxM9, BxM11), which carry 65,000+ daily riders, with connections to the 2, 3, 6, B, C trains and seven perpendicular bus routes. The study area experiences slow bus speeds, with buses traveling less than 4 mph in some segments. Weekday congestion causes 785 hours of delay to M116 passengers daily. 116th Street is a Vision Zero Priority Corridor, within a Priority Youth Injury Area and Senior Area. NYC DOT aims to improve safety through organizing the roadway, improving visibility and predictability, slowing turning vehicles, and creating safer crossings.

The study area experiences slow bus speeds, with buses traveling less than 4 mph in some segments. Weekday congestion causes 785 hours of delay to M116 passengers daily. 116th Street is a Vision Zero Priority Corridor, within a Priority Youth Injury Area and Senior Area. NYC DOT aims to improve safety through organizing the roadway, improving visibility and predictability, slowing turning vehicles, and creating safer crossings.

The proposed improvements include a two-way protected bike lane linking Riverside Park and the Hudson River Greenway to Central Park, bus boarding islands at bus westbound bus stops, and a dedicated signal phase for pedestrians and cyclists crossing Central Park West. title: 79th Street, Riverside Drive to FDR Drive
link_text: 79th Street, Riverside Drive to FDR Drive - presented to Manhattan Community Board 7 in April 2025 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is planning to install transit and pedestrian safety improvements along 79th Street from Riverside Drive to the FDR Drive as part of the 79th Street SBS Capital Project. This capital project follows up on NYC DOT’s 2017 Street Improvement Project (SIP) that was implemented as part of the launch of the M79 Select Bus Service. Improvements made by this capital projects will include bus bulbs, upgraded bus stops, new bus pads, updated ADA elements, curb extensions, improved median pedestrian refuges, refurbished sidewalks, stormwater infiltration basins, and new landscaping. The safety benefits of the project will include increased pedestrian visibility and accessibility, shorter and safer pedestrian crossings, and slower and safer vehicle turns. The transit benefits of the projects include the provision for faster boarding and alighting times, improved bus reliability, and new bus stop amenities.

title: Amsterdam Avenue, Laurel Hill Terrace to West 188th Street
link_text: Amsterdam Avenue, Laurel Hill Terrace to West 188th Street - Street Design Checklist (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements on Amsterdam Avenue, between Laurel Hill Terrace and W 188th Street. This school safety project aims to improve safety for students from the 10 schools located on Amsterdam Avenue. This project will narrow the road to slow speeding vehicles and prevent reckless driving, provide a dedicated place for cyclists, shorten pedestrian crossings, and improve visibility at the intersections. The proposal includes a two-way protected bike lane along the east curb of Amsterdam Avenue from Laurel Hill Terrace to W 188th Street. The project also includes painted curb extensions and pedestrian islands throughout, as well as concrete bus boarding islands at W 184th Street and W 187th Street to improve bus stop accessibility. Additionally, this project proposes converting W 187th Street from Laurel Hill Terrace to Amsterdam Avenue to one-way westbound, reducing turn conflict with pedestrians and cyclists.

title: Broadway Vision, Union Square to Columbus Circle
link_text: Broadway Vision Design Update - presented to Manhattan Community Board 5 in September 2026 (pdf)
description: Since 2009, NYC DOT has continued to promote the use of Broadway as public space by promoting walking and biking as the primary mode of transportation on this world-renowned corridor. As part of this ongoing work, NYC DOT has developed a comprehensive vision for a vibrant and safe Broadway from Union Square to Columbus Circle which supports local commerce, community, and culture. Through a flexible toolkit, the Broadway Vision includes block typologies from basic, to slow, to shared, to pedestrianized plazas that can be organized to meet a variety of stakeholder needs, amplifying the public realm of each unique neighborhood while building a cohesive transportation network. In 2024, NYC DOT implemented a new plaza between East 17th Street and East 18th Street, as well as shared street blocks from East 18th Street up to East 21st Street using in-house resources. NYC DOT is currently working on design concepts for Broadway between West 35th Street and West 38th Street. In coordination with NYC DDC, NYC DOT is currently in the design stage for capital improvements to the existing plaza and shared street blocks between West 38th and West 40th Streets. Additional capital projects are in the early stages of development and more information on those projects will be added as they progress.

title: Central Park Drives
link_text: Central Park Drives - Status Update - presented to Manhattan Community Boards 8 and 7 in January 2026 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is planning a repaving and redesign of the Central Park Drives to improve safety and comfort for pedestrians and cyclists. The redesign builds on recommendations from the Central Park Drives Safety and Circulation Study released in 2024, for more clearly designated space for pedestrians and cyclists along the park’s six-mile loop road. The proposed improvements include allocating space consistently across the drives for different users groups, providing better separation between pedestrians and cyclists, and modifying the signals to clearly designate them for cyclists to improve compliance. This year’s project includes the southern portion of the drives from W 96th Street on the west side to E 90th Street on the east side. The repaving of the northern section of the park loop will take place next year after the reconstruction of The Davis Center is complete.

title: Flatiron Plaza & Shared Street
link_text: Flatiron Plazas and Worth Square - presented to Manhattan Community Board 5 in September 2026 (pdf)
description: The Flatiron Plazas were implemented using interim materials in 2008. The plazas (Broadway/5th Avenue between 21st and 25th Streets) were an important milestone in NYC DOT’s efforts to enhance pedestrian accessibility and have transformed what was a congested, traffic dominated and hostile environment into a landmark public space. In 2017 NYC DOT refreshed the plazas and implemented a series of enhancements focused on public space, pedestrian safety and circulation whilst maintaining vehicular circulation. These proposals simplified the complex intersection of Broadway/5th Avenue/24th St, added a new protected bike lane on Broadway and 5th Avenue and converted the block of Broadway between 25th and 24th Streets into a Shared Street. NYC DOT is now working with NYC DDC to develop the final design for the permanent reconstruction of the plazas, shared street and Worth Square. There will be upcoming public engagement this year. The preliminary design was presented to Community Board 5 on March 4th, 2019. The Major Concession ULURP Application was presented to Community Board 5's Land Use Committee in February 2026.

title: Lafayette Street/4th Avenue, Astor Place, East 8th Street, West 13th Street

title: Jamaica Bay Greenway
link_text: Jamaica Bay Greenway Presentation (pdf)
description: The Jamaica Bay Greenway is a planned 28-mile network of pedestrian and bicycle paths connecting communities along the Jamaica Bay waterfront to more than 10,000 acres of city, state and federal parkland, including Rockaway Beach, Marine Park, Canarsie Pier, Floyd Bennett Field and the Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge. More than 10 miles of the Greenway already exist, serving roughly 100,000 local and regional visitors annually. When completed, multi-use paths and on-street bicycle markings will create a loop route around Jamaica Bay, allowing cyclists and walkers to commute, exercise and explore the Bay’s natural beauty from Sheepshead Bay and Spring Creek in Brooklyn to Howard Beach and the Rockaway Peninsula in Queens. description: NYC DOT is proposing Vision Zero safety improvements on Liberty Avenue, between Merrick Boulevard and Sutphin Boulevard, in Queens. This corridor is home to York College/Queens High School for the Sciences, industrial and commercial businesses, and is nearby Jamaica Center transit hub. Proposed improvements include one new concrete pedestrian refuge island, concrete median tips/pedestrian refuges, concrete and painted curb extensions, left turn traffic calming treatments, and updated roadway markings along the entire corridor. These treatments will improve safety by encouraging safer speeds, increasing pedestrian visibility and yielding by drivers, shortening crossing distances with safe places to rest, and encouraging slower, safer turns.

title: Little Neck Parkway & Nassau Boulevard
link_text: Little Neck Parkway & Nassau Boulevard - What's Happening Here? Flyer
description: NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements at the Vision Zero Priority Intersection of Little Neck Parkway and Nassau Boulevard in Queens. This project will add four painted curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances for pedestrians and encourage slower, safer turns at the intersection. This proposal also upgrades markings and adds quick kurb to the intersection to further encourage safer speeds and turns and improve yielding.

title: Myrtle Wyckoff Plaza and Wyckoff Avenue Corridor Safety Improvements
link_text: Wyckoff Avenue Intersection & Plaza Corridor Safety Improvements - presented in November 2024
description: Three pedestrian fatalities between 2009 and 2014 occurred at this complicated six-leg intersection on the border of Brooklyn and Queens, at the bustling Myrtle/Wyckoff transportation hub. In 2014, NYC DOT implemented five turn bans which saw low compliance. In 2016, new Vision Zero safety funding presented an opportunity to further simplify the intersection. The 2016 project converted Wyckoff Avenue between Gates and Myrtle into a pedestrian plaza, which allowed pedestrians to make subway to bus connections without crossing the street and created a central neighborhood public space where the Myrtle Avenue and Wyckoff Avenue retail corridors intersect. In conjunction with NYC DDC, NYC DOT is planning to construct the temporary plaza in permanent materials as part of a larger NYC DEP sewer and water main replacement project. The permanent plaza will feature additional street furnishings, pedestrian scale lighting, and landscaping.

link_text: Thomson Avenue, 44th Drive to Van Dam Street, 44th Drive, 23rd Street to Thomson Avenue - presented to Queens Community Board 2 in September 2026 (pdf)

title: Thomson Avenue, Skillman Avenue to VanDam Street
link_text: Thomson Avenue / Skillman Ave to VanDam St - presented to Queens Community Board 2 in February 2016 (pdf)
description: Thomson Avenue falls within a Vision Zero Priority Area with many pedestrian generators on a constrained south sidewalk, an underutilized north sidewalk and substandard moving lanes that process a high volume of vehicular traffic. NYC DOT developed this capital plan to reallocate sidewalk from the north to the south and to mark standard width moving lanes.

title: Union Turnpike, 251st Street to 266th Street
link_text: Union Turnpike, 251st Street to 266th Street - presented to Queens Community Board 13 in April 2026 (pdf)
description: NYC DOT is proposing safety improvements on Union Turnpike between 251st Street and 266th Street. Union Turnpike is a six lane corridor, it is also a truck route, with 5 MTA bus lines operate. The major land use along the corridor are mixed of residential and commercial. The potential project improvements include several slip road closures, street direction changes, median closures, and curb extensions to reduce turn conflicts and enhance pedestrian safety, reduce pedestrian crossing distance, increase pedestrian space and transit loading areas.

title: Woodhaven Boulevard, Queens Boulevard to 107th Avenue
link_text: Woodhaven Boulevard, Queens Boulevard to 107th Avenue - presented to Queens Community Board 9 in December 2024
description: NYC DOT is proposing transit and pedestrian safety improvements along Woodhaven Boulevard in Queens, from Queens Boulevard to 107th Avenue. The proposed improvements would be installed as part of three separate capital projects, beginning with the Woodhaven Boulevard Phase B capital project (from Union Turnpike to 107th Avenue), which is estimated to start construction in 2026. Improvements made by these capital projects will include curb extensions, median widenings, raised crosswalks, and new landscaping. The safety benefits of the projects include increased pedestrian visibility and accessibility, shorter and safer pedestrian crossings, and slower and safer vehicle turns. The transit benefits of the projects include the provision for faster boarding and alighting times, improved bus reliability, and new bus stop amenities.
